=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~26134-26141 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The support-aware cap skip uses `contains($support)`, which matches the substring ` support=<sha> ` anywhere in the comment body instead of restricting it to the cap marker's `support=` field. An older cap marker in a comment body can therefore satisfy the check whenever PR-controlled text in the same body (e.g. the `cap_first_error` line copied from the workflow failure log, or any other body text the PR's commit/PR history can shape) happens to contain the literal substring ` support=<current support SHA> `.
  WHY: The whole point of issue #6625 is to let a support-script fix release previously capped PRs. The Python helper `count_identical_failures` (`scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` ~2238-2276) does this correctly by parsing the marker fields via `_marker_fields(_FAILURE_CAP_MARKER_RE.search(...))` and comparing `fields.get("support")`. The shell path diverges and accepts `contains($support)`, so when a comment already carries an older cap marker AND PR-controlled text echoes the current support SHA, the poller treats the older cap as current and skips redispatch (`NOOP_RECOVERY_SKIP_FINGERPRINT_CAP`), leaving the affected PR blocked despite updated review support. The new `STALE_SUPPORT` log only fires when the loose check correctly fails, which means the safety net is bypassable. The test coverage (`test_cap_skip_other_support_version_redispatches`, `test_fingerprint_cap_block_marker_records_support_version`) only exercises comments whose body contains the cap marker in isolation, so this divergence is not pinned.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~2519-2526 (the `fingerprint-cap-block` job's "already applied" jq query) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Same trust-boundary looseness in the cap-block job's `AUTOFIX_FINGERPRINT_CAP_ALREADY_APPLIED` early-out: `(.body // "") | contains(" support=" + $support + " ")`. The check finds a comment that carries the cap marker prefix for this head and then verifies ` support=<sha> ` appears anywhere in the body, rather than parsing the marker's `support=` field.
  WHY: When the gate trips on a new support SHA but an older cap marker exists for the same head and the comment body also contains the substring ` support=<new SHA> ` (from `cap_first_error` copying failure-log text, or any PR-controlled text echoed into the cap comment), the cap-block job's early-out fires, the new cap marker is never posted,
